title: Forgetting .Value on Value Objects
summary: IntValue/StringValue/etc. are CONTAINERS — the data is in .Value. Using the object itself in math, comparisons, or Text silently fails: 'attempt to perform arithmetic on Instance', or always-false comparisons.

explanation.whatItIs: The box-vs-contents mixup: you wanted the number inside the box but handed over the box.
explanation.whyItExists: Value objects exist to put plain data in the instance tree; their 'data port' is .Value.
symptoms: coins + 1 → 'attempt to perform arithmetic on an Instance value'
if coins == 100 then — never true (Instance ≠ number)
label.Text = coins → 'Coins' or a weird printout/error
explanation.fix: Touch the data port: coins.Value + 1; if coins.Value >= 100; label.Text = tostring(coins.Value).
tips: Same rule for StringValue (.Value), ObjectValue (.Value = the Instance), BoolValue
Attributes avoid the wrapper entirely: GetAttribute returns the raw value
commonMistakes: Mixing .Value and bare usage in one system — pick a convention
Writing leaderstats updates without .Value and seeing frozen scores

examples.title: Box vs contents
examples.code:
local coins = player.leaderstats.Coins   -- IntValue (the box)

-- ❌
-- coins += 10
-- if coins >= 50 then

-- ✅
coins.Value += 10
if coins.Value >= 50 then
    print("Rich! Total:", coins.Value)
end
